name: Alpha Invariance / Inverse Scaling
aliases: Inverse scaling between distance and volume density
definition: A property where the alpha value (opacity) of a discretized segment remains constant despite changes in scene scale, achieved by inversely scaling the volume density σ(x) relative to the distance (interval length) along the ray.
summary: Alpha Invariance maintains constant opacity under scene scaling by inversely adjusting volume density relative to distance, ensuring visual consistency across arbitrary scales unlike fixed-discretization methods.
